faq.q: Can foreigners own an Indian company?
faq.a: Foreign ownership is possible in many sectors, subject to India's FDI policy and applicable approval requirements.

faq.q: Which business structure should we choose?
faq.a: It depends on your business activities, ownership and future plans. We help compare permitted options.

faq.q: How long does incorporation take?
faq.a: The timeline depends on document readiness, name approval and MCA processing; we'll provide an indicative schedule.

faq.q: Can incorporation happen remotely?
faq.a: Often, yes, subject to identity verification, signing and document formalities.

faq.q: What documents do overseas owners need?
faq.a: Typically identity, address, incorporation and authorisation documents, depending on the ownership structure.

faq.q: Do we need an Indian resident director?
faq.a: Indian companies must meet the applicable resident-director requirement. We can explain compliant options.

faq.q: How does foreign investment get reported?
faq.a: Applicable forms and deadlines depend on the investment transaction. We help identify and complete the required reporting.

faq.q: How long does bank onboarding take?
faq.a: It varies by institution, KYC review and ownership structure. Bank approval is independent.

faq.q: Can the company operate immediately after incorporation?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Banking, commencement requirements and activity-specific registrations may still be needed.

faq.q: What ongoing compliance is required?
faq.a: Applicable obligations may include corporate filings, accounting, tax, audit and foreign investment reporting.

faq.q: Can you manage ongoing local operations?
faq.a: Yes. Accounting, payroll, tax and corporate compliance support can be scoped as an ongoing engagement.

faq.q: Do you advise private and public companies?
faq.a: Yes. We support applicable corporate law and governance matters for private companies, public companies and LLPs. Sector-specific requirements are assessed separately.

faq.q: How is a secretarial audit different from a compliance review?
faq.a: A statutory audit follows specific legal requirements; a voluntary review identifies compliance gaps. Remediation is scoped separately where independence requires it.

faq.q: Can you handle annual ROC filings?
faq.a: Yes, including applicable corporate filings and related secretarial processes under an agreed scope.

faq.q: What approvals are needed to issue new shares?
faq.a: Requirements vary by the share issue route and investor type. We assess the structure and prepare an approval checklist.

faq.q: Can a company convert a loan into equity?
faq.a: Sometimes. The route depends on loan terms, prior approvals and applicable corporate and foreign investment rules.

faq.q: Can shareholding change without selling business assets?
faq.a: Often, yes. Share transfers, issues and other corporate actions may be possible, subject to review.

faq.q: Can you review shareholder or share purchase agreements?
faq.a: Yes, for applicable company law and governance matters, coordinating specialist legal counsel when needed.

faq.q: What should we do after receiving an ROC notice?
faq.a: Check the deadline, gather records and obtain advice before responding. We can assess the notice and support the response.

faq.q: What is the difference between compounding and adjudication?
faq.a: They are different statutory processes for certain offences or monetary penalties. The applicable process depends on the provision and facts.

faq.q: Can you review company records before an investment?
faq.a: Yes. We assess relevant incorporation, capital, filing and governance records and report findings.

faq.q: Can we engage you for a single matter?
faq.a: Yes. One-off advice, specific transactions and longer-term retainers can be scoped separately.

faq.q: How is a share purchase different from a business transfer?

faq.q: Does my business need NBFC registration?
faq.a: This depends on your principal activities and the applicable RBI rules. We can help assess your position.

faq.q: What capital is needed to register an NBFC?
faq.a: Requirements vary by NBFC category and current RBI regulations. We review the applicable threshold for your proposal.

faq.q: How long does RBI registration take?
faq.a: Timelines depend on eligibility, documentation and RBI review; approval cannot be guaranteed.

faq.q: What recurring filings does an NBFC need?
faq.a: This depends on your classification and activities and may include RBI returns, Companies Act filings and governance requirements.

faq.q: Do ownership changes require RBI approval?
faq.a: Certain ownership, control and management changes do. We recommend checking before proceeding.

faq.q: What is Scale-Based Regulation?
faq.a: It is an RBI framework that sets obligations based on an NBFC's classification and relevant criteria.

faq.q: Can GAA handle ongoing compliance?
faq.a: Yes. Reporting, secretarial, policy and governance support can be included in an agreed engagement.

faq.q: Can overseas investors invest in an NBFC?
faq.a: Potentially, subject to the applicable foreign investment and RBI requirements.
